note: Labeled, explicit-code, hyphen-range, explicit period -- the fully clean happy path.
Bare $ never establishes currency; no period marker stays unavailable. Only numeric bounds resolve.
Ordinary ungrouped integer (no comma grouping at all) is a supported numeric form.
£ is unambiguous (GBP only); repeated on both operands of a to-range.
€ is unambiguous (EUR only); between...and range form.
Explicit open-lower form sets minimum only; maximum is never fabricated.
Explicit open-upper form sets maximum only.
Hyphenated 'up-to' spelling is an approved synonym of 'up to'.
A bare anchored single amount sets minimum == maximum (not an open-ended floor).
Label's trailing colon is optional.
Bare 'salary' (no colon, lowercase) is still a recognized closed-catalog label.
Label matching is case-insensitive.
A trailing k on only the last operand of a range shares backward onto the unmarked first operand.
Exact zero-fraction .00 combined with k-scaling: 120.00 (exact) then x1000.
Exact .00 fractional suffix is accepted; never rounded, just recognized as zero-fraction.
Fullwidth digits (U+FF10-FF19) NFKC-normalize into ASCII range before matching.

Arabic-Indic digits do not NFKC-fold to ASCII and are rejected by the explicit [0-9] grammar -- a lexical mismatch (no production fullmatches), landing in Table D (all four fields unavailable), not a semantic numeric failure.
Non-Western grouping (groups of 2 after the leading group) is rejected, not guessed.
A valid 1-3-digit leading group followed by a non-3-digit group is still malformed.
Exceeds PostgreSQL's 32-bit signed integer maximum; rejected, not clamped.
Boundary case: exactly the int32 maximum is valid (the check is > max, not >= max).
Boundary case: one over the int32 maximum is rejected.
No legitimate negative salary; a negative sign always invalidates its operand.
A textually-reversed range is never silently reordered; both bounds become unavailable.
Nonzero decimal on the FIRST operand nulls BOTH bounds atomically; the clean $20 is never promoted to a standalone match. Explicit USD code proves currency/period genuinely survive.
Negative sign on the FIRST operand nulls both bounds atomically; currency/period survive.
Malformed grouping on the FIRST operand nulls both bounds atomically; currency/period survive.
Overflow on the SECOND operand nulls both bounds atomically; the clean $120,000 first operand is never promoted to a standalone match.
Atomicity proven on the 'to' separator, first-operand failure (decimal).
Atomicity proven on the 'to' separator, second-operand failure (overflow).
Atomicity proven on the 'between...and' separator, first-operand failure (decimal).
Atomicity proven on the 'between...and' separator, second-operand failure (overflow).
An explicit but unsupported period word (enumerated catalog) invalidates numeric extraction too; currency still survives independently.
An unenumerated 'per word' still lexically fills the period slot via the generic fallback, and is semantically unsupported the same way; currency survives.
$ is compatible with an explicit USD code.
$ is compatible with an explicit CAD code.
$ is compatible with an explicit AUD code.
$ conflicts with an explicit GBP code -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds and period (a supported synonym is included) both survive.
$ conflicts with an explicit EUR code -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds and period survive.
£ is compatible with an explicit GBP code (redundant but consistent).
£ conflicts with an explicit USD code -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds and period survive.
€ is compatible with an explicit EUR code (redundant but consistent).
€ conflicts with an explicit GBP code -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds and period survive.
Two different explicit codes (prefix USD, suffix CAD) conflict -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds and period survive.
An explicit code alone (no symbol at all) both anchors and resolves currency.
Two different symbol types on the two operands conflict -- currency unavailable, numeric bounds unaffected (same general mechanism as the code-conflict cases, not a separate special case).
'bonus' cannot be consumed by any production slot, so the whole field fails to fullmatch -- all four fields unavailable, no separate keyword scan needed.
'plus equity' is not the bare '+' open-lower marker and is not consumable -- whole field fails to fullmatch.
'total compensation' is not in the closed label catalog and is not a period/code -- whole field fails to fullmatch.
A second candidate range elsewhere in the text leaves unconsumed leftover content -- whole field fails to fullmatch.
Unknown leftover semantic text after a valid-looking amount disqualifies all four fields; no substring is scanned out of the larger unsupported statement.
No currency symbol, code, or label anywhere -- an unrelated number is never confidently read as salary.
A structurally-valid range with no anchor at all (no symbol/code/label) is still rejected -- the anchor requirement applies to every shape, not only bare singles.
A bare unanchored number, even zero, is never extracted.
Zero is a valid nonnegative integer once anchored; not treated as missing.
No numeric candidate at all; 'Compensation' is also not in the closed label catalog.
Only a single trailing period is the enumerated harmless-punctuation allowance; two periods are left as unconsumed leftover text.
Empty string safely resolves to all-unavailable.
Whitespace-only string normalizes to empty and safely resolves to all-unavailable.
A None compensation_text (field genuinely absent) safely resolves to all-unavailable.
The 'to' separator requires whitespace on both sides; a glued 'to$' form fails to fullmatch under any production, rather than silently matching a malformed shape.
The overflow guard is a PostgreSQL int32-safety bound, not a subjective 'realistic salary' ceiling -- a large but in-range value is accepted.
A bare $ symbol alone anchors extraction even with no label/code; a tightly-glued period suffix (no space) is supported.
Period resolves independently of currency in a clean (non-failure) case: bare $ leaves currency unavailable while period still resolves.

Period synonym catalog: '/hr' -> hourly, tightly glued.

Codex round-4 correction 2: a label without a colon requires at least one covered-whitespace character before what follows; a glued form is never accepted.
Codex round-4 correction 2: label glued directly to a currency symbol is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 2: multi-word label glued directly to a currency code is rejected.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_label_no_colon_glued: the same label with the required covered-whitespace boundary present.
Codex round-4 correction 3: a currency code glued directly to the amount is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 3: an amount glued directly to a trailing currency code is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 3: the label:colon boundary allows zero whitespace, but the code-to-amount boundary still requires it -- rejected.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_code_prefix_glued: the same code with the required covered-whitespace boundary present.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_code_suffix_glued: the same code with the required covered-whitespace boundary present.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_label_colon_code_glued: the code-to-amount boundary is still spaced even though the label:colon boundary is optional.
A label with a colon may be followed by zero covered whitespace (approved, distinct from a label without a colon, which requires at least one).
Codex round-4 correction 4: a word-based period glued directly to the amount is rejected -- only slash forms may attach directly.
Codex round-4 correction 4: a 'per X' period glued directly to the amount is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 3+4 combined: both the code and the period boundary are glued -- rejected.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_word_period_glued: a slash-form period is approved to attach directly to the amount with no covered whitespace.
Positive control neighboring correction_reject_per_period_glued: the same 'per year' form with the required covered-whitespace boundary present.
Codex round-4 correction 5: only 'up' + whitespace + 'to' or literal 'up-to' are approved -- a doubled hyphen is neither and is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 5: a mixed space-then-hyphen separator is not one of the two approved forms and is rejected.
Codex round-4 correction 5: a mixed hyphen-then-space separator is not one of the two approved forms and is rejected.
